# Copy to .env for local overrides (gitignored). `make up` uses .env if present, otherwise this file.
ENV=dev

# --- Postgres (P1 stack: host port 5544; the spike stack keeps 5543) ----------
# kg_app: NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, used by the API and worker. kg_owner: runs migrations only.
DATABASE_URL_APP=postgresql+psycopg://kg_app:kg_app_dev@127.0.0.1:5544/kg
DATABASE_URL_OWNER=postgresql+psycopg://kg_owner:kg_owner_dev@127.0.0.1:5544/kg
# Integration tests run against this separate database (same server, same roles).
TEST_DATABASE_URL_APP=postgresql+psycopg://kg_app:kg_app_dev@127.0.0.1:5544/kg_test
TEST_DATABASE_URL_OWNER=postgresql+psycopg://kg_owner:kg_owner_dev@127.0.0.1:5544/kg_test
TEST_SCRATCH_DATABASE_URL_OWNER=postgresql+psycopg://kg_owner:kg_owner_dev@127.0.0.1:5544/kg_scratch
KG_APP_PASSWORD=kg_app_dev
KG_OWNER_PASSWORD=kg_owner_dev
POSTGRES_ADMIN_PASSWORD=kg_admin_dev

# --- Neo4j (P1 stack: bolt 7688, browser 7475) --------------------------------
NEO4J_URI=bolt://127.0.0.1:7688
NEO4J_USER=neo4j
NEO4J_PASSWORD=kg-neo4j-dev

# --- Model router: mock (default) or live -------------------------------------
OSO_ROUTER_MODE=mock
# The live router is reached ONLY through its public address (HTTPS), from the host and from containers alike: no local port, no host.docker.internal.
# Containers use http://mock-router:8781/v1 in mock mode (compose sets that); a router key is needed for live mode and is never committed.
OSO_ROUTER_MOCK_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8782/v1
OSO_ROUTER_LIVE_URL=https://models.oso.group/v1
# Separate keys per service so spend is attributable. Never commit a real key.
OSO_ROUTER_API_KEY_API=mock-key
OSO_ROUTER_API_KEY_WORKER=mock-key
MOCK_ROUTER_API_KEY=mock-key
MODEL_PURPOSES_PATH=compat/model-purposes.yaml
PRICING_PATH=compat/pricing.yaml

# --- Auth (dev values; ENV=production refuses these defaults) -----------------
AUTH_KEY_PEPPER=dev-only-pepper-change-me-32-bytes-min
AUTH_JWT_SECRET=dev-only-jwt-secret-change-me-32-bytes
AUTH_JWT_TTL_SECONDS=900
TELEMETRY_HMAC_SECRET=dev-only-telemetry-secret

# --- Observability --------------------------------------------------------------
LOG_LEVEL=INFO

# --- Agents (P7) ----------------------------------------------------------------
# The registration API (POST/PATCH/DELETE /v1/principals...). false: manage principals with the CLI only (`kg principals`).
PRINCIPAL_API_ENABLED=true
# Platform default for a principal whose registration sets no limit (in-process; the shared limiter is P9).
PRINCIPAL_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE=1200
# The MCP server (apps/mcp) needs only these; it has no database or router setting by design.
KG_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000
MCP_HOST=127.0.0.1
MCP_PORT=8010
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=
GRAPHITI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false
SEMAPHORE_LIMIT=8

# --- Graph projection (P2, moved onto the outbox in P3) -----------------------------
# Commands enqueue a graph_projection job in their own transaction; the worker's outbox dispatcher runs it (the P2 sweeper was deleted in P4).
# How long a command request waits for its own projection before answering 202 with a status URL.
PROJECTION_REQUEST_BUDGET_SECONDS=5

# --- Interaction ledger and outbox (P3) -----------------------------------------------
# Payload encryption at rest: AES-256-GCM keyring "kid:base64(32 bytes),kid:base64(32 bytes)". New writes use PAYLOAD_ACTIVE_KID; old kids stay readable
# until `kg payloads reencrypt` moves their rows. ENV=production refuses the development key. Generate one:  python -c "import os,base64;print(base64.b64encode(os.urandom(32)).decode())"
PAYLOAD_KEYS=dev1:ZGV2LW9ubHktcGF5bG9hZC1rZXktMzItYnl0ZXMtISE=
PAYLOAD_ACTIVE_KID=dev1
# HKDF master for the per-workspace keyed content hash (request hashes, content hashes). Separate from the payload keys so rotating them never breaks idempotent replay.
CONTENT_HMAC_SECRET=dev-only-content-hmac-secret-32-bytes
INTERACTION_MAX_CONTENT_BYTES=262144
# Outbox dispatcher. Lease and backoff are judged by the database clock.
WORKER_CONCURRENCY=4
WORKER_STAGE_LIMITS=graph_projection=2
WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS=30
WORKER_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS=20
# Test-only failure injection (never in production; the validator refuses it): KG_FAULTS="normalize:after_claim:3"; KG_FAULTS_DIR holds counters and a `spec` file.
KG_FAULTS=
KG_FAULTS_DIR=

# --- Extraction, identity and review (P4) ----------------------------------------------
# Identity candidates: name trigram similarity and E5 cosine of the name embeddings. Placeholders until `make eval-extraction-live` records the real
# distributions (ADR-013: E5 similarities cluster high, so the cosine floor is high).
IDENTITY_TRGM_MIN=0.45
IDENTITY_COS_MIN=0.92
# Graphiti keeps the episode text in Neo4j so later extractions can use it as context. Neo4j sits inside the trusted data boundary; false blanks it after extraction.
GRAPH_STORE_EPISODE_CONTENT=true
# Earlier episodes sent as extraction context. 0 = every interaction is extracted on its own (deterministic, and no cross-interaction content in a prompt).
GRAPH_PREVIOUS_EPISODES=0
CONTEXT_TOKEN_MARGIN=0.85
compat/model-purposes.yaml:
# Purpose -> router alias map (Phase 0 §2.3). The platform refers to PURPOSES, never models.
# Status: PROVISIONAL until `make live-session-apply`. `make verify-router` ran against https://models.oso.group on 2026-10-19 (LV-04 / GR-12):
#   oso/general and oso/fast answer 422 unsupported_capability to response_format json_schema; oso/code, oso/code-high and oso/frontier answer valid JSON;
#   oso/reasoning was inconsistent (invalid JSON once, 503 routing_failed once). So every STRUCTURED purpose uses oso/code with oso/code-high as fallback, and only
#   plain-text purposes stay on oso/general / oso/fast. If the router admin adds an `oso/structured` alias (router-contract section 11), change these lines only.
# Source for alias and capability facts: oso_model_router scripts/seed-logical-router.ts (ALIASES, DEPLOYMENTS).
version: 1
status: accepted
model_purposes:
  graph_extraction:
    alias: oso/code                 # -> oso/structured if the router admin creates it (docs/router-contract.md section 11)
    requires: [structured_output]
    fallback_alias: oso/code-high
    task_type: extraction
  graph_extraction_small:
    alias: oso/code                 # NOT oso/fast or oso/general: neither supports structured output on the live router (422 unsupported_capability)
    requires: [structured_output]
    fallback_alias: oso/code-high
    task_type: extraction
  memory_extraction:
    alias: oso/code
    requires: [structured_output]
    fallback_alias: oso/code-high
    task_type: extraction
  memory_consolidation:
    alias: oso/code                 # P8: a condensed group of memories, validated sentence by sentence and ALWAYS reviewed (ADR-043)
    requires: [structured_output]
    fallback_alias: oso/code-high
    task_type: summarization
  ontology_simulation:
    alias: oso/code                 # P8: extraction of sample interactions under a DRAFT ontology, in an isolated staging namespace (ADR-046)
    requires: [structured_output]
    fallback_alias: oso/code-high
    task_type: extraction
  graph_projection:
    alias: oso/embedding            # embedding-only: deterministic command projections write nodes/edges directly and never call a chat model (ADR-016)
    requires: []
    task_type: embedding
  context_compression:
    alias: oso/fast                 # P6 'summarized' mode only; plain text output
    requires: []
    task_type: summarization
  embedding:
    alias: oso/embedding
    dim: 384
    max_input_tokens: 512           # model limit (e5-small); the router advertises 8192, which is the deployment figure
    prefix:
      query: "query: "
      passage: "passage: "
    embedding_model_id: intfloat/multilingual-e5-small
    embedding_version: 1

# Egress policy (SEC-06 / ING-06): which data classifications may be sent to the router at all.
# `local_only` is never sent: the standard router setup has no local deployment and rejects it with data_policy_violation.
egress:
  allowed_classifications: [public, internal, confidential, restricted]
  denied_classifications: [local_only]
  on_denied: skipped_by_policy
docs/adr/ADR-012-model-gateway-and-route:
# ADR-012: Model gateway and router contract

**Status:** Accepted (live session 2026-10-21)  **Decision refs:** DEC-02, SEC-06, ING-06
**Evidence:** G-01..G-04, MR-01, GR-02, GR-05 · `docs/router-contract.md`, `compat/model-purposes.yaml`, `tools/mock_router`, `spikes/gateway`

## Context
All LLM and embedding traffic goes through the user's Oso Model Router (OpenAI-compatible, chooses the physical model, ledger-side cost). The router's actual behaviour differs from vanilla OpenAI in ways that break common libraries.

## Decision
1. **One `ModelGateway`** is the only code that talks to the router. Callers name a **purpose** (`graph_extraction`, `memory_extraction`, `context_compression`, `embedding`), never a model or alias. `compat/model-purposes.yaml` maps purposes to aliases and is the only place aliases appear.
2. **Chat completions only.** The router has no `/v1/responses`; Graphiti's default `OpenAIClient` (Responses API) fails against it (GR-02), so Graphiti is constructed with `OpenAIGenericClient` in `json_schema` mode. Everything it sends (`model, messages, temperature, max_tokens, response_format`) survives the router's schema.
3. **Never rely on dropped fields:** `logprobs`, `top_logprobs`, `logit_bias`, `seed`, `n` are stripped silently, so logprob rerankers and seeded determinism are unavailable (ADR-019 search recipes avoid the cross-encoder).
4. **Egress is checked before the call.** Classes in `egress.denied_classifications` (`local_only`) raise `EgressDenied`; the call is never sent (asserted with a transport spy, G-02) and the stage becomes the terminal, non-error **`skipped_by_policy`**. Router policy errors map to the same state.
5. **Error categories:** retryable (`rate_limited, provider_unavailable, timeout, unknown_provider_error, routing_failed`) back off exponentially with `Retry-After` taking precedence and a bounded attempt count (default 4); policy-terminal → `skipped_by_policy`; config-terminal → operator alert, no retry; budget → pause the queue. An exhausted retryable primary falls back to the purpose's `fallback_alias` once; budget/policy/config errors never fall back (G-03).
6. **Metadata for joinability, never content:** `x-request-id` = platform `correlation_id` (must be a UUID or the router ignores it), `application_id=kg-platform`, `task_type`, `data_classification`, and HMACs of principal and workspace. The call log is metadata-only (purpose, alias, tokens, latency, router request id, estimated cost, tokenizer).
7. **Cost is estimated locally** from `compat/pricing.yaml` (alias → primary candidate; a floor when fallback fires) because the response carries no cost; the router ledger stays authoritative.
8. **Structured output:** `oso/fast` has no eligible model; `oso/general` has exactly one (gemini-3.5-flash). Initial map: `graph_extraction`/`memory_extraction` → `oso/general`, fallback `oso/code`. Change request to the router admin: an **`oso/structured`** alias (glm-5.2 → gemini-3.5-flash → gemini-3.8-flash → gemini-3.1-pro-preview).
9. **Cost of Graphiti (offline call counts through the mock, Sarah episodes with the compiled ontology):** evt_001 = 4 chat calls, evt_002 = 5, evt_003 = 8, each with roughly 6–8 embedding calls. Chat calls grow with existing edges (dedupe/contradiction and timestamp calls). Token cost and latency per episode are GR-11.
10. **Use a non-admin key per service** (`kg-api`, `kg-worker`): admin keys expose provider/model headers and defeat attribution.

## Consequences
The mock router is a first-class test tool (49 contract tests) so P1–P6 never need the live router; the live kit turns this ADR from Provisional to Accepted.

## Live follow-up (what changes this ADR)
LV-04/GR-12 decide the alias map or the `oso/structured` request; LV-06 decides whether platform keys need a higher `maxClassification`; GR-13 sets `SEMAPHORE_LIMIT`; GR-11 sets expected cost per episode.
docs/adr/ADR-013-embeddings.md:
# ADR-013: Embeddings

**Status:** Accepted (live session 2026-10-21)  **Decision refs:** DEC-08 (part), DEC-02
**Evidence:** G-04, PV-04, GR-02, GR-10, MR-01 · `docs/router-contract.md` §6

## Context
`oso/embedding` resolves to `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small` on Vertex (us-central1 only, no fallback, router-advertised 8192-token context, model limit 512).

## Decision
1. **384 dimensions.** pgvector columns are `vector(384)`; Graphiti's embedder uses `embedding_dim=384`; the gateway asserts the length of every returned vector (G-04). A mismatch is a hard error.
2. **E5 prefixes.** Platform memory search embeds queries with `query: ` and stored memories with `passage: ` (asymmetric). **Graphiti's embedder cannot distinguish query from passage**, so its wrapper uses `query: ` on both sides (E5's recommendation for symmetric tasks). The wrapper also handles Graphiti passing a one-element list (found in GR-02).
3. **Chunking.** Inputs are split into ≤ (512 − prefix − 2) token windows by the gateway and the chunk vectors are mean-pooled and re-normalised; the result records `chunked=True`. This never relies on the router to truncate (LV-05 will show what it does).
4. **Versioning.** Every vector row stores `embedding_model_id`, `embedding_dim`, `embedding_version` with `CHECK (vector_dims(embedding) = embedding_dim)`. Same-dimension model changes are re-embedded in batches under a new version and reads are pinned to the current version; dimension changes use add-column / backfill / swap (PV-04). **Graphiti stores its own embeddings in Neo4j**, so a model change is one "embedding generation" change covering both stores.
5. **Single deployment risk.** Embeddings have no router fallback; a write that needs an embedding is retried by the worker and the stage stays retryable (`*_failed` is not terminal). Optional router change request: a second 384-dim deployment.
6. **Thresholds are not portable.** Graphiti's `sim_min_score=0.6` is tuned for other embedding models; E5 similarities cluster high, so thresholds must be re-tuned from live data (LV-05 records related vs unrelated cosine).

## Live follow-up
LV-05: observed dimension, >512-token behaviour (silent truncation vs error), cosine ranges. If E5-small proves too weak for entity matching (GR-11), the fix is the version mechanism above plus a router change, not a code redesign.
docs/adr/ADR-020-tokenizer-auth-networki:
# ADR-020: Tokenizer and budget accounting; dev auth; dev networking

**Status:** Accepted for dev auth and networking; tokenizer margin calibrated by TK-02 (live session 2026-10-21)  **Decision refs:** CTX-01, DEC-03  **Evidence:** TK-01, AU-01, NW-01

## Tokenizer and budget (CTX-01)
- The router picks the model, so the platform counts **its own output** (the context package), not router calls.
- **Count = ceil(max(o200k_base, cl100k_base) × 1.10)** using tiktoken. The two agree within 1% on English/JSON/UUID text but cl100k_base counts ~47% more on multilingual text, so the larger is used; a `chars/4` heuristic under-counts structured text (JSON, UUIDs, dates) by up to 60% and is forbidden for hard budgets.
- The tokenizer id string (`tiktoken:max(o200k_base,cl100k_base)+margin0.1`) is recorded in every context trace.
- The 10% margin is **provisional**: TK-02 measures router `prompt_tokens` for the same samples on each alias and raises the margin until the platform count ≥ observed for 100% of samples.

## Dev auth (DEC-03)
- Platform-issued API keys `kgk_<8-char prefix>_<secret>`: stored as prefix + SHA-256(pepper‖key), constant-time compare, optional expiry, immediate revocation (no cache layer), prefix displayed in the admin UI, plaintext shown once. Principals are workspace-bound; the workspace comes from the key record or token claim, **never** from a header or body.
- Optional 15-minute JWT (HS256, local signer) after key exchange. Rejected in tests: tampered claims, `alg=none`, wrong key, wrong audience, missing `workspace_id`, expired, algorithm confusion.
- **Library: PyJWT** (small, algorithms must be pinned, required-claim enforcement). authlib is an OAuth framework we do not need.
- **OIDC path (documented, not built):** verify RS256/ES256 against the IdP's JWKS (`PyJWKClient`), pin algorithms, require `iss/aud/exp`, map a configured claim (or group→workspace table) to `workspace_id`. The `Principal` shape is unchanged, so no other code moves.

## Dev networking (NW-01)
> **Superseded 2026-10-19 (owner decision):** the platform reaches the router only at `https://models.oso.group/v1`, from the host and from containers. The loopback / `host.docker.internal` arrangement below is history; it also does not work on Linux for a loopback-published router (tested: connection refused). See `docs/router-contract.md` section 12.

- The router binds `127.0.0.1` only. Verified on macOS Docker Desktop: a container reaches a host-loopback-only service through `http://host.docker.internal:<port>`, and a container's own `127.0.0.1` does not.
- Defaults: `OSO_ROUTER_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8780/v1` for host-run processes, `http://host.docker.internal:8780/v1` for containerised api/worker, with `extra_hosts: ["host.docker.internal:host-gateway"]` in compose for Linux CI. Do **not** rebind the router to `0.0.0.0`. Fallback if Docker Desktop changes behaviour: run api/worker on the host in dev.
- Not yet verified against the real router process (it was not running during the offline run); LV-01 and `make verify-router` from a container cover it.
